newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Former Ecuador minister to help with Cyprus talks.
newsitem.headline: Former Ecuador minister to help with Cyprus talks.

text.p: Ecuador's former foreign minister Diego Cordovez has been appointed as a special adviser to Secretary-General Kofi Annan to help with expected talks between leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.
Cordovez takes up his new U.N. post on April 28.
His appointment followed an announcement that the secretary-general's special representative for Cyprus, Han Sung-joo of South Korea, would not continue in that position beyond the end of this month.
"The secretary-general is determined to press ahead with intensified efforts to bring about a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus issue," the U.N. spokesman said.

"The secretary-general hopes that the current process will lead to direct talks between the two leaders within the next two months," he added, referring to President Glafcos Clerides, as head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974, when Turkish troops landed in the north of the island after a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
The United Nations has been trying for decades to reunite the island under a federal system.
Cordovez was a U.N. staff member for 25 years and, as an under-secretary-general in the 1980s, conducted negotiations that led to the withdrawal of Soviet troops from Afghanistan.
He was Ecuador's foreign minister from 1988 to 1992 and then was appointed diplomat-in-residence at New York's Columbia University.
